purpose: Generic apply/recovery/trace behavior checks on multi-step unseen tasks, proving the split is behavior-preserving for state-machine invariants.

generic_checks.shape: an unseen multi-hunk diff applied through the new apply/ path
generic_checks.assertion: result identical to old path (byte-for-byte tree state)

generic_checks.shape: the same recovery action driven twice on an unseen task
a duplicate action with a reused consumer_event_id on an unseen task
an unseen task producing N trace events
generic_checks.assertion: causal ordering identical old vs new; consumer correlation intact

generic_checks.shape: enumerate all state-machine transitions exercised by an unseen flow
generic_checks.assertion: transition set identical old vs new (no add/remove/rename)

generic_checks.shape: an apply that should fail (conflicting hunk) on an unseen input
generic_checks.assertion: fails identically old vs new; failure reported with F1 class

generation_rule: unseen multi-step tasks and diffs generated fresh; the invariant is identical old-vs-new behavior on state, ordering, idempotence, and duplicate protection
